description: Build/contract: EE registers the SCIM provider while CE exposes no functioning endpoint.
Integration: Pro and higher can administer and call SCIM; sub-Pro and entitlement-lost tenants are rejected without state mutation.
Permission integration: security-settings read/update permissions independently gate viewing and mutating SCIM configuration.
Credential integration: token plaintext is returned once, only a hash persists, timing-safe verification works, and raw secrets never enter logs.
Credential lifecycle: replacement token overlaps with the old token, traffic succeeds on both during overlap, and revocation immediately rejects the selected token.
State guard: disabling SCIM preserves connection data, links, active users, inactive users, and history while rejecting runtime operations.
Protocol contract: ServiceProviderConfig, Schemas, and ResourceTypes accurately advertise Users-only supported capabilities.
Protocol integration: Users lookup supports userName, externalId, resource ID, pagination, SCIM media types, and stable metadata.
Protocol failure table: invalid filter, malformed payload, unknown ID, invalid token, disabled connection, and temporary failure return sanitized standard SCIM errors.
DB-backed happy path: POST exact-email matches one existing active internal user, creates one link, returns a SCIM resource, and creates no Alga user.

DB-backed match guards: no match, duplicate match, client user, inactive user, already-linked user, and alias/UPN/display-name/fuzzy/domain-inferred near-matches fail without user or link mutation and upsert unresolved records.
DB-backed tenant isolation: an identity cannot discover, match, link, read, or mutate a user or link in another tenant.
Reconciliation integration: administrator resolves an unresolved exact or mismatched identity with required warning, permission, and audit history.
DB-backed uniqueness/concurrency: repeated and concurrent POST requests produce one stable link and never reassign either identity.
Attribute authority: PUT and PATCH update observed email/profile drift while leaving every Alga-controlled user, authorization, license, and notification field unchanged.
DB-backed deactivation: active=false sets user inactive, stores SCIM provenance, revokes all tracked sessions, and records a sanitized operation.
Authentication integration: after successful SCIM deactivation, a previously valid session is denied on its next protected request through another application instance.
DB-backed reactivation: active=true reverses SCIM-applied inactivity and preserves all existing roles, teams, permissions, and assignments.
DB-backed source guard: active=true does not reactivate a manually inactive user, including under retries and concurrent updates.
DB-backed DELETE: deprovisioning revokes sessions, tombstones the link, and preserves the user, roles, assignments, and representative historical records.
Lifecycle retry matrix: duplicate PUT, PATCH, active transitions, and DELETE requests return stable effective state without duplicate side effects.
User-management integration: SCIM-managed status appears, upstream inactive blocks activation with guidance, unlinking preserves effective state, and warnings are accurate.
UI flow: Pro administrator enables SCIM, views the token once, copies Entra guidance, rotates/revokes credentials, sees health state, and is rejected when attempting to configure a second connection.
UI data flow: linked-user and unresolved-identity views show identity, source, upstream/effective state, drift, operation status, and resolution controls.
Audit/security: setup, rotation, revocation, manual link, unlink, deactivate, reactivate, and delete events are sanitized and attributable.
Rate-limit integration: abusive connection/source traffic is throttled without affecting another tenant or exposing connection validity.
Emulator E2E: deterministic assignment performs lookup and POST, disable revokes access, reassign reactivates, and delete soft-deprovisions.
Emulator resilience: token rotation, duplicate delivery, concurrency, stale replay, timeout, interruption, malformed PATCH, bad schema, and bad filter produce expected idempotent outcomes.
Build boundary: emulator code and dependencies are absent from production EE server artifacts.

Live Entra acceptance: Test Connection, exact-email link, unmatched failure, disable/unassign, session rejection, reassign, drift, DELETE, and token rotation pass against a test enterprise application.
Documentation contract: published guidance covers supported tier, setup mappings, exact-email policy, unsupported Groups, lifecycle behavior, rotation, errors, and recovery.
